correctness.rationale: The continuum claim is proved by exact quotient inequalities, not inferred from enumeration. Two-entity and one-seat cases are excluded analytically; the three-entity/two-seat cell is excluded by an averaging contradiction; the two minimal failure chambers follow from the necessary and sufficient conditions that the dominant entity's last selected quotient exceed every rival first quotient together with the upper-quota inequality. The probability formulas are exact simplex integrals. The embedded exact-rational checker reproduces the discrete allocations, divisor certificates, witness minimality, and both integrals.

value.rationale: Upper quota is a central apportionment fairness axiom and Jefferson/D'Hondt is a canonical divisor method. The coordinatewise-minimal failure cells are mathematically natural boundary objects: they identify the first dimensions in which the method's large-entity bias can cross upper quota. The complete chambers, exact neutral-simplex probabilities, and unique least-total integer witnesses turn a qualitative known defect into a sharp local classification.
